official.title: Postdoc Position in Quantum Control of Semiconductor Qubits
official.description_text:
Join the Veldhorst Group, pioneers in germanium-based quantum computing and simulation.
Job description
After a successful first hire for this research topic, we are looking for a second Postdoctoral Researcher to join the Veldhorst Group, who are pioneers in quantum computing and simulation in germanium. The Veldhorst group demonstrated the first single-hole qubit, enabled two-qubit logic in germanium, and executed quantum algorithms on a four-qubit quantum processor.
As a Postdoc researcher, you will explore opportunities with semiconductor quantum technology and aim to push the boundaries in quantum control of semiconductor qubits.
The Veldhorst group is a collaborative and supportive research environment where team members work closely together, share expertise, and mentor one another while advancing the field of semiconductor quantum technology.
Near-term projects include multi-qubit operation, entanglement generation between qubit registers, and multi-quantum wells for higher dimensional quantum systems.
Requirements
You have a PhD degree in physics, applied physics, nanoelectronics or comparable discipline at the time of taking on the position. Prior experience in solid-state quantum computing, spin qubits, or superconducting qubits would be beneficial but is not required.
Doing a Postdoc at TU Delft requires English proficiency at a certain level to ensure that the candidate is able to communicate and interact well, participate in English-taught Doctoral Education courses, and write scientific articles and a final thesis. For more details please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements.
TU Delft (Delft University of Technology)
Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference.
For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future.
At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward.
QuTech
At QuTech, we work on radically new technologies with world-changing potential. Our mission: to develop scalable prototypes of a quantum computer and a quantum internet by integrating world-class research and groundbreaking innovation. Through excellence, relevance, and leadership, we cultivate a vibrant quantum technology ecosystem. Together, we are creating the quantum future, because we believe that quantum technologies can be a game changer in many societal and economic sectors, including health, agriculture and safety.
Have a look at our
video
and get a glimpse of QuTech.
Conditions of employment
Duration of contract is 4 years.
A job of 38-40 hours per week.
Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities. The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged.
Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit,
Coming to Delft Service
, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A
Dual Career Programme
is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands.
Additional information
If you would like more information about this vacancy or the selection procedure, please contact Menno Veldhorst, via
M.Veldhorst@tudelft.nl
.
For questions about the procedure, please contact our Senior Recruiter Audrey Monje at
A.Monje@tudelft.nl
.
Application procedure
Are you interested in this vacancy? Please apply no later than
15 November 2026
via the application button and upload the following documents:
CV
Motivational letter
You can address your application to Menno Veldhorst.
Please note:
You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post.
A pre-employment screening can be part of the selection procedure.
As part of knowledge security, TU Delft conducts a risk assessment during the recruitment of personnel. We do this, among other things, to prevent the unwanted transfer of sensitive knowledge and technology. The assessment is based on information provided by the candidates themselves, such as their motivation letter and CV, and takes place at the final stages of the selection process. When the outcome of the assessment is negative, the candidate will be informed. The processing of personal data in the context of the risk assessment is carried out on the legal basis of the GDPR: performing a public task in the public interest. You can find more information about this assessment on our website about
knowledge security.
Please do not contact us for unsolicited services

ai.summary: TU Delft postdoc position in quantum computing within the Veldhorst Group, focussing on multi-qubit operations, entanglement generation, and higher-dimensional quantum systems using germanium-based semiconductor qubits. Requires PhD in physics or nanoelectronics with prior quantum computing or spin-qubit experience.

thematic_fit.rationale: Quantum computing, semiconductor physics, and spin-qubit control have no thematic connection to human-centred XR, immersive learning, spatial cognition, wayfinding, or collaborative systems. This is pure quantum technology research. The exclusion rule applies: 'pure ML algorithm development' is excluded; quantum algorithm implementation sits in the same category of pure technical specialisation orthogonal to HCI and human-centred immersive research.

methodological_fit.rationale: Quantum control research employs experimental physics, device characterisation, and algorithm validation—none of which align with HCI, user studies, or experimental design for human behaviour and learning. The researcher has no background in quantum mechanics, solid-state physics, or qubit control. Methodological distance is maximal.

growth_value.rationale: Pursuing a quantum computing postdoc would represent a complete departure from the researcher's target identity and strategic goal. No transferable capability. This would not close gaps in spatial cognition research, immersive system design, advanced user-study methodology, or collaborative-systems evaluation—the areas the researcher needs to build for a human-centred XR PhD.

strategic_value.rationale: While TU Delft is a priority-1 institution and QuTech is well-funded, the research group (Veldhorst Group) operates in a completely different scientific ecosystem. The researcher would gain exposure to stable Horizon Europe-adjacent funding and a rigorous research environment, but zero strategic value toward the target identity. Would require a fundamental re-definition of research goals.

eligibility_flags: Position requires PhD in physics, applied physics, nanoelectronics, or comparable discipline. Researcher's MSc is in Multimedia from a Creative Faculty; disciplinary fit is unclear and likely weak.
Prior experience in quantum computing or spin qubits is described as beneficial but not required. Researcher has zero background in either.
No mention of immersive systems, HCI, user research, or interactive design in the posting.
risks: Career misalignment: accepting this role would signal to the HCI and immersive-systems communities that the researcher is pivoting away from human-centred XR. This would damage credibility and network-building in the target field.
Skill transferability: quantum physics skills do not transfer to immersive-systems research. The researcher would return to the PhD job market without progress on core human-centred methods.
Disciplinary isolation: joining a quantum computing group at a physics-heavy institution could marginalise the researcher from HCI and design-science communities.

PhD readiness: a quantum postdoc would not strengthen the researcher's candidacy for human-centred immersive-systems doctoral positions. Potential PhD advisors in HCI/XR would view this as evidence of scattered research identity.

eligibility_reasons: whether a completed degree is required before employment is not stated; your MSc is still in progress — verify with the source
